title: SkyHarbor Air: A Complex Airline Seeking Decision-Grade Intelligence
executive_summary: SkyHarbor Air operates across passenger, cargo, loyalty, maintenance, and digital domains with significant evidence gaps.
what_context_reveals: Planning-grade context exists; operational, financial, and vendor evidence remains largely unvalidated across key domains.
why_it_matters: Without reconciled baselines, AI transformation investments risk misalignment between ambition and defensible outcomes.
decision_implication: No board-defensible business case should advance until cross-system lineage and finance sign-off are established.
evidence_still_needed: Validated baselines across IROPS, crew, maintenance, baggage, and managed-services domains are not yet evidenced.
module_usage: Knowledge surfaces enterprise profile; Tower validates baselines; Source scopes sourcing readiness.
next_validation_action: Commission a cross-domain evidence audit covering operations, finance, and vendor contracts before any initiative advances.

title: Global Airline with Multi-Domain Complexity and Legacy Exposure
executive_summary: SkyHarbor Air spans passenger, cargo, loyalty, airport, maintenance, and digital operations with inherited legacy system debt.
what_context_reveals: Enterprise scope is broad; system consolidation from prior integrations has left duplicated legacy instances unresolved.
why_it_matters: Legacy duplication increases operational risk, inflates managed-services cost, and slows analytics modernization timelines.
decision_implication: A consolidated system inventory is prerequisite to any rationalization, sourcing, or AI-readiness program.
evidence_still_needed: Consolidated system inventory across legacy instances is not yet evidenced; needs validation before scope decisions.
module_usage: Knowledge builds enterprise profile; Tower validates system inventory; Source scopes rationalization candidates.
next_validation_action: Request a verified system inventory covering all legacy instances inherited from prior integrations.

title: Operations, Commercial, and Support Functions Operate with Fragmented Handoffs
executive_summary: Flight ops, crew, stations, cargo, loyalty, and contact center functions lack system-mediated handoffs during disruptions.
what_context_reveals: Network and station views reconcile by phone rather than system, creating decision latency during irregular operations.
why_it_matters: Phone-mediated reconciliation during IROPS events amplifies recovery cost and degrades customer experience outcomes.
decision_implication: System-mediated handoff evidence must precede any AI-assisted disruption decision support deployment.
evidence_still_needed: System-mediated handoff between ops control and stations is not yet evidenced; needs operational validation.
module_usage: Knowledge maps business function dependencies; Tower validates handoff evidence; Operations surfaces disruption lineage.
next_validation_action: Document and validate the current handoff process between network operations control and station teams.

title: Decision Rights Between Operations and IT Remain Unresolved
executive_summary: No joint governance forum with real authority exists; ops and IT decision ownership is contested across key programs.
what_context_reveals: Interview signals confirm unresolved decision-ownership is a structural blocker for IROPS and data governance programs.
why_it_matters: Without chartered decision rights, AI recommendations lack accountable owners and cannot clear safety or compliance gates.
decision_implication: A documented decision-rights model signed by ops and IT leadership is prerequisite to any AI program advancement.
evidence_still_needed: Chartered joint governance forum with decision authority is not yet evidenced; needs executive sponsorship.
module_usage: Knowledge surfaces ownership gaps; Tower validates governance charter; Nexus tracks accountability assignments.
next_validation_action: Charter a joint ops-IT governance forum with explicit decision authority before next program milestone.

title: Frontline Trust Eroded by Prior Tool Failures; Adoption Risk Is High
executive_summary: Prior tool failures have reduced frontline confidence; deployment is being reported as adoption without utilization evidence.
what_context_reveals: Interview signals flag that deployment metrics are substituted for adoption metrics in executive reporting.
why_it_matters: Overstating adoption masks real utilization gaps and undermines the value case for AI-assisted workflows.
decision_implication: Post-launch utilization reporting at ninety days must be mandatory before any tool is declared operationally adopted.
evidence_still_needed: Hub-level pilot with logged override rate and ninety-day utilization report are not yet evidenced.
module_usage: Knowledge profiles workforce readiness; Tower validates utilization evidence; Operations tracks override telemetry.
next_validation_action: Require a ninety-day post-launch utilization report for every deployed tool before adoption is claimed.

title: Application Landscape Is Fragmented with Unreconciled Legacy Instances
executive_summary: Reservations, DCS, crew, baggage, and maintenance systems span legacy and target-state platforms without certified inventory.
what_context_reveals: AWS lakehouse and modernization platforms are target-state; current-state certification is not yet evidenced across domains.
why_it_matters: Uncertified application inventory prevents defensible sourcing scope, migration planning, and AI integration design.
decision_implication: No sourcing or migration decision should proceed without a finance-certified current-state application inventory.
evidence_still_needed: Current-state application inventory certified across legacy and target-state platforms is not yet evidenced.
module_usage: Knowledge maps application landscape; Tower validates inventory; Source uses certified scope for sourcing readiness.
next_validation_action: Commission a certified application inventory covering all operational domains before sourcing scope is defined.

title: Cross-System Data Lineage Is Uncertified Across All Operational Domains
executive_summary: Flight, crew, baggage, maintenance, and finance data flows lack certified lineage, blocking decision-grade analytics.
what_context_reveals: No reconciled cross-system cost view of IROPS days exists; OTP recovery metric is used unvalidated across pitches.
why_it_matters: Unvalidated metrics used in board materials create audit exposure and undermine executive credibility.
decision_implication: Tower-validated metric definitions and cross-system lineage proof must precede any board-level analytics claim.
evidence_still_needed: Cross-system lineage proof from DCS, crew, and finance is not yet evidenced; needs Tower validation.
module_usage: Knowledge catalogs data assets; Tower validates lineage and metric definitions; Operations surfaces integration gaps.
next_validation_action: Initiate a Tower-led lineage validation sprint covering DCS, crew, finance, and baggage data flows.

title: Target Lakehouse Is Aspirational; Current Infrastructure Certification Is Absent
executive_summary: AWS airline data lakehouse is a target-state platform; current infrastructure readiness for analytics workloads is unvalidated.
what_context_reveals: Maintenance analytics and baggage analytics use cases depend on lakehouse certification not yet in evidence.
why_it_matters: Deploying analytics use cases on uncertified infrastructure creates reliability, latency, and data-quality risk.
decision_implication: Infrastructure certification must precede any production analytics deployment on the target lakehouse.
evidence_still_needed: AWS lakehouse certification for production analytics workloads is not yet evidenced; needs platform validation.
module_usage: Knowledge profiles infrastructure; Tower validates platform readiness; Operations assesses latency and reliability evidence.
next_validation_action: Request a platform readiness assessment for the target lakehouse before analytics use cases are promoted.

title: Vendor Landscape Carries Concentration Risk and Unexamined Renewal Exposure
executive_summary: GDS, AMS, and legacy platform vendors represent concentration risk without a board-ready concentration ratio view.
what_context_reveals: GDS distribution cost is creeping upward unexamined; GDS renewal and data migration decisions are made in isolation.
why_it_matters: Isolated renewal decisions without joint contract-and-migration risk modeling create avoidable cost and lock-in exposure.
decision_implication: A vendor concentration ratio report and joint contract-migration risk model are needed before any renewal proceeds.
evidence_still_needed: Vendor concentration ratio by system category and multi-year GDS cost trend analysis are not yet evidenced.
module_usage: Knowledge maps vendor relationships; Source scopes contract optimization; Tower validates concentration evidence.
next_validation_action: Produce a vendor concentration ratio report by system category for audit committee review.

title: IT Spend Is Untraceable to Outcomes; Capital Plan Lacks Spend Visibility
executive_summary: Invoices do not code to projects; conflicting baselines across business cases prevent defensible value measurement.
what_context_reveals: ROI cases bundle hard savings with speculative gains; no single reconciled cost baseline is finance-approved.
why_it_matters: Bundled ROI cases and untraced invoices expose the organization to audit risk and misallocated capital.
decision_implication: Invoice-to-project coding remediation and a disaggregated business case standard are required before capital approval.
evidence_still_needed: Finance-approved capital plan tied to spend visibility and reconciled cost baseline are not yet evidenced.
module_usage: Knowledge surfaces spend gaps; Tower validates baseline and invoice evidence; Source uses certified spend for sourcing.
next_validation_action: Remediate invoice-to-project coding and require finance sign-off on all business case baselines.

title: Program Portfolio Lacks Auditable Baselines and Reconciled Control Artifacts
executive_summary: IROPS, crew, maintenance, baggage, and analytics programs advance without co-existing baseline and control artifacts.
what_context_reveals: Baseline and control artifact rarely co-exist on one initiative; sponsor-only value cases go unaccountable.
why_it_matters: Programs without joint baseline-plus-control artifacts cannot demonstrate realized value or satisfy audit requirements.
decision_implication: A uniform gating checklist requiring joint baseline and control artifact must apply to every program regardless of AI label.
evidence_still_needed: Joint reconciled baseline plus control artifact for each active program is not yet evidenced.
module_usage: Knowledge catalogs programs; Tower validates gating evidence; Nexus tracks milestone accountability.
next_validation_action: Apply a uniform gating checklist requiring joint baseline and control artifact before any program milestone is approved.

title: AI Ambition Outpaces Evidence; No Auditable End-to-End Pilot Event Exists
executive_summary: IROPS copilot, crew recovery, agent assist, and maintenance analytics are planning-grade; none have auditable pilot events.
what_context_reveals: Planning speed is being conflated with production readiness; no single logged, human-reviewed IROPS event is on record.
why_it_matters: Promoting planning-grade AI use cases as production-ready creates safety, compliance, and credibility risk.
decision_implication: One logged, human-reviewed, outcome-compared IROPS event must exist before any AI use case is promoted to operations.
evidence_still_needed: Auditable end-to-end pilot event with human review and outcome comparison is not yet evidenced for any use case.
module_usage: Knowledge profiles AI use cases; Tower validates pilot evidence; Operations governs human-in-the-loop controls.
next_validation_action: Execute and log one complete IROPS pilot event with human review and outcome comparison before next board review.

title: Passenger-Rights Obligations and Safety Controls Are Not Coded into AI Recommendations
executive_summary: AI recommendations for rebooking and crew recovery do not yet encode passenger-rights obligations or safety controls.
what_context_reveals: Human-review gate evidence is absent; budget pressure is threatening the human-in-the-loop safeguard design.
why_it_matters: Customer-facing AI without encoded obligations creates regulatory, reputational, and liability exposure.
decision_implication: A protected funding line for human-in-the-loop design and a human-review gate must precede any customer-facing automation.
evidence_still_needed: Human-review gate evidence and protected human-in-the-loop funding line are not yet evidenced.
module_usage: Knowledge surfaces risk and control gaps; Tower validates control evidence; Operations governs safety gate design.
next_validation_action: Establish and fund a human-review gate before any passenger-facing AI recommendation is deployed.

title: Managed-Services and GDS Relationships Lack Governance Depth and Exit Clarity
executive_summary: AMS and GDS relationships carry ambiguous exit rights, benchmarking gaps, and unvalidated AI automation commitments.
what_context_reveals: Termination assistance, step-in rights, and benchmarking provisions need legal validation before any renegotiation.
why_it_matters: Renegotiating without validated exit rights and benchmarking evidence weakens leverage and increases transition risk.
decision_implication: Legal review of exit, benchmarking, and AI automation commitments must precede any managed-services renegotiation.
evidence_still_needed: Legal-validated exit rights, benchmarking provisions, and AI commitment terms are not yet evidenced.
module_usage: Knowledge maps relationship context; Source scopes contract optimization; Tower validates legal and SLA evidence.
next_validation_action: Commission legal review of exit rights, benchmarking, and AI automation clauses across all managed-services agreements.

title: Evidence Sources Are Synthetic and Planning-Grade; No Certified Operational Data Exists
executive_summary: All contracts, invoices, tickets, and interview signals are synthetic planning-grade evidence, not certified operational records.
what_context_reveals: No realized savings, SLA credits, or operational improvement outcomes are claimed or evidenced at this stage.
why_it_matters: Treating synthetic planning evidence as certified operational data creates false confidence in business case quality.
decision_implication: Every evidence source must be explicitly classified as planning-grade or certified before it informs a board decision.
evidence_still_needed: Certified operational evidence across all domains is not yet evidenced; classification audit is needed.
module_usage: Knowledge catalogs evidence sources; Tower validates certification status; Nexus tracks evidence classification.
next_validation_action: Conduct an evidence classification audit distinguishing planning-grade from certified sources across all active programs.

title: Key Metrics Are Unvalidated and Used Inconsistently Across Executive Materials
executive_summary: OTP recovery, recovery cost per event, and crew shortfall cost metrics are used without Tower-validated definitions.
what_context_reveals: Unvalidated metrics appear across board materials and business cases, creating audit and credibility exposure.
why_it_matters: Inconsistent metric definitions prevent meaningful performance comparison and undermine board-level decision quality.
decision_implication: Tower-validated metric definitions must be established and locked before any metric appears in board materials.
evidence_still_needed: Tower-validated definitions for OTP recovery, recovery cost per event, and crew shortfall cost are not yet evidenced.
module_usage: Knowledge surfaces metric gaps; Tower validates definitions and lineage; Nexus tracks metric governance status.
next_validation_action: Initiate Tower-led metric validation for OTP recovery, recovery cost, and crew shortfall before next board cycle.

title: Airline Industry Patterns Amplify IROPS, Managed-Services, and Legacy Risk
executive_summary: Irregular-operations sensitivity, managed-services dependency, and legacy reservations are characteristic airline risk amplifiers.
what_context_reveals: Industry patterns suggest IROPS cost exposure and managed-services concentration are structurally above average for this profile.
why_it_matters: Industry-pattern awareness helps prioritize evidence collection where airline-specific risk is highest and fastest-moving.
decision_implication: IROPS, managed-services, and legacy platform evidence should be prioritized given industry-pattern risk amplification.
evidence_still_needed: Benchmarked industry-pattern comparison for IROPS cost and managed-services concentration is not yet evidenced.
module_usage: Knowledge applies industry context; Tower validates against benchmarks; Source uses patterns for sourcing leverage.
next_validation_action: Apply airline industry benchmarks to IROPS cost and managed-services concentration before next sourcing review.

title: Operations, Finance, and Legal Lenses Are Not Yet Jointly Applied to Any Initiative
executive_summary: No initiative has simultaneously applied operations, finance, and legal expert lenses to validate its evidence base.
what_context_reveals: Value cases are sponsor-driven; finance and legal sign-off are absent from most active program baselines.
why_it_matters: Single-lens value cases create blind spots in risk, compliance, and financial defensibility.
decision_implication: A joint ops-finance-legal review must be required for every initiative before it advances to board-level approval.
evidence_still_needed: Joint sponsor-finance-legal sign-off on any active initiative baseline is not yet evidenced.
module_usage: Knowledge surfaces expert lens gaps; Tower coordinates multi-lens validation; Nexus tracks sign-off status.
next_validation_action: Require joint ops, finance, and legal sign-off on every initiative baseline before board submission.

title: Managed-Services Scope Is Unvalidated; SLA and Invoice Evidence Are Unreconciled
executive_summary: AMS and IMS scope lacks certified CMDB, SLA history, SOW mapping, and invoice-to-rate-card reconciliation.
what_context_reveals: Service-credit eligibility, chronic SLA misses, and change-order leakage are hypotheses without reconciled evidence.
why_it_matters: Unreconciled managed-services evidence prevents defensible renegotiation and exposes the organization to leakage.
decision_implication: CMDB, SLA, SOW, invoice, and rate-card evidence must be reconciled before any renegotiation or re-sourcing proceeds.
evidence_still_needed: Finance-certified SLA history, invoice-to-SOW reconciliation, and rate-card variance analysis are not yet evidenced.
module_usage: Knowledge profiles managed-services scope; Source scopes renegotiation readiness; Tower validates SLA and invoice evidence.
next_validation_action: Reconcile SLA history, invoices, and SOW mapping across all managed-services towers before renegotiation scope is set.

title: Operational Process Evidence Is Fragmented Across IROPS, Baggage, and Maintenance Domains
executive_summary: IROPS lineage, baggage scan completeness, and maintenance work-order reconciliation are unproven across operational domains.
what_context_reveals: Outstation baggage data reconciles a day late; maintenance event lineage and parts feeds are not certified.
why_it_matters: Day-late reconciliation and uncertified maintenance lineage prevent real-time decision support and reliability analytics.
decision_implication: Network-wide real-time scan coverage and certified maintenance lineage must precede any operational analytics deployment.
evidence_still_needed: Real-time bag scan coverage proof and certified maintenance event lineage are not yet evidenced.
module_usage: Knowledge surfaces process evidence gaps; Tower validates operational lineage; Operations governs data quality controls.
next_validation_action: Validate network-wide real-time bag scan coverage and certify maintenance event lineage before analytics deployment.
